title: ID0371713-DC/Si-D/FI[MP / P8 170000823] - Jämsä Fuse -FC14 tripped.
description:
Location: Jämsä, Finland
Reported behavior/issue:
Charger was offline. 26.7.2024 Plugit technician found out that the fuse -"FC14" was tripped and red (See Video in timeline).
Technician reset the fuse and it stayed ON. When technician was charging his EV, fuse tripped again and he couldnt reset it anymore. During the troubleshooting, we found out that it was possible to reset “-FC14” when right LEM-meter supply was disconnected from “+F11-XD21” connector 3A. Main unit right socket is disabled and LEM-meter supply is disconnect.
Seems like the LEM is defected but I will continue troubleshooting 31.7.2024.
Root cause:
Solution:
Loose wire connection found; issue fixed during site visit

additional_info.subject: ID0371713-DC/Si-D/FI[MP / P8 170000823] - Jämsä Fuse -FC14 tripped. CRM:00315001654
additional_info.body:
Hi Markus,
After our short meeting, you explained to me how there was already a troubleshooting task performed where the FC14 was tripped and trialed removing the 24V cable from each device pertaining to the FC14 (router1, router2, LEM1, LEM2, HMI and Switch) and only when you remove the LEM2 meter from this FC14, it was able to be turned ON again and workable.
For my perspective, there is somehow a surge of current on one of these devices, from your explanation, it seems like the LEM2 meter is provoking the issue, since we can see in the logs that when we charge with DC2, suddendly we lose logs → FC14 trip.
So my recommendation is to go on-site, perform a charging session in DC2 and wait for it to trip. If it trips, then let's trial again removing the 24V and see if it comes back to green when removing LEM2.
If it is as explained above I would like to trial the same test but changing the connection of LEM2 to FC12 and retry this.
If it works then it is most likely that the component is workable but somehow it has some problem that is causing the current surge.
If it doesn't work then we have a faulty LEM meter and needs to be replaced.
Please take a spare LEM to site and some 24V cables for the rewiring.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.body:
Hi Markus, good morning.
After the site visit, we were able to understand that the problem might come from the HMI actually and not the LEM. When we power ON, FC14 is RED and cannot be reseted unless we remove 24V from the XD21:4C (24V HMI).
You measured the resistance from the FC14 to ground and it has a very low value of 800ohm. What I measured in the Training Center is in kiloOhm.
I will go back there today to confirm the value which we should have. If there is a leakage we must investigate it.
Let's keep in touch for the next steps. When are you planning to return there?
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0371713-DC/Si-D/FI[MP / P8 170000823] - Jämsä Fuse -FC14 tripped. CRM:00315001654
additional_info.body:
Hi Markus,
After today's site visit, as soon as you arrived, you measured again the resistance from XD21 and found no issue.
When we removed the 24V from the HMI and replugged, the FC14 tripped again. The resistance was not as bad as previously (idea is that the probes were not inserted tightly in the terminals, I also faced this issue when I measured in our charger), we have a good resistance but after we plug in the 24V HMI, the resistance suddenly drops and keeps dropping.
This, in theory, indicates that the HMI is requesting a lot of current and that's why the resistance is dropping since the capacitance is high.
Since you didn't have a Clamp current meter, I cannot accept the values you registered since I used the same multimeter as you and faced different values from using the clamp meter.
In any case, just a gut feeling but the capacitors in the HMI are discharging too fast (or related) and that's why we see the surge of current, resulting the FC14 tripping and that's why sometime afterwards of FC14 being able to be reset we are able to continue since the current requested is less, since the other devices are already powered on.
From my perspective, here are the next actions:
Measure the current,
with the clamp meter
, from the HMI when starting up the charger → from the measurement I made in our charger it should be ~0.2A
Recommend you to order a new HMI and take it to site in case we find that the current requested is above what I measured.
As you mentioned, since you don't have the clamp meter and the HMI, we will postpone this to when you are back.
As such I  will assign this ticket to you.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
